new_topics.name: Agent privacy becomes a runtime governance problem
new_topics.summary: Treat privacy for autonomous agents as a runtime systems problem spanning memory, logs, tool access, cross-agent handoffs, consent and deletion propagation.
new_topics.why_now: MLCommons released v0.1 of its Agent Privacy Risk Taxonomy, defining five agent-specific data-protection areas and a path toward benchmark development.
new_topics.practical_value: Gives deployers a concrete checklist for data minimization, context sharing, deletion propagation and accountability before agent workflows reach sensitive systems.
new_topics.limitations: The taxonomy is an early draft and does not yet provide validated benchmark scores or deployment-specific risk rankings.
new_topics.next_action: Track MLCommons benchmark work and test whether representative agent workflows minimize data, propagate deletion requests and preserve policy across handoffs.

updates.what_changed: Cloudflare Clef and Clef-flash add an independent open-weight, Jev-compatible implementation of typed probabilistic decision models.
ThinkingBox adds executable terminal-state and side-effect checks across repeated trials, directly testing when an agent's completion claim diverges from the system outcome.
Anthropic's three-tier Cyber Verification Program adds deployed evidence for capability and safeguard levels matched to verified users and risk context.

no_drop_justification: No active topic crossed the archival threshold in this bounded sweep; unchanged topics still retain unresolved next-action tests or prior evidence and no contrary signal justified removal.
